timeline.message:
Warn on slow signature verification

Plugin downloads can sometimes take unexpectedly
long because of slow random number generation on certain
operating system versions, e.g. Debian based OS
distros with kernels older than 5.6. This PR adds
a warning message for users explaining why plugin
installation from remote URLs is taking unexpectedly long.
timeline.author: Nikola Grcevski

timeline.body:

timeline.body: Hi @grcevski, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Why not have this timer be local to computeSignatureForDownload?

reply.body: The main reason I split it this way is to be able to mock computeSignatureForDownload, but I really like your suggestion, there's no reason to pollute the mainline of that code with the timer block. I'll extract into a method that signifies that we are wrapping with a timer.

timeline.body: Can we just block here indefinitely? I'm concerned for flakiness if this completes within the same slice, and the wrong thread unblocks first, that this could appear "ok" and cause the test to fail.

That seems like a very generic exception to depend on, which could mask another problem (an actual NPE). Why would we not expect the install to succeed in this case? Can't we mock it in such a way that it works?

reply.body: Yeah valid point, I think I can make this work. Right now my mock method for computeSignatureForDownload is simply a sleep call, so the verification doesn't happen and a later call fails with NPE. But I can do the work of the original method too after the sleep and then it will succeed just fine.

timeline.body:
If we're suggesting changing to `/dev/urandom` I think we should spell out how to do that here. I'd rather we said to fix `/dev/random`, avoiding that whole problem, but I'd mostly be ok with either. How about this wording?

> The plugin installer is trying to verify the signature of the downloaded plugin
but this verification is taking longer than expected. This is often because the
plugin installer is waiting for your system to supply it with random numbers.
Ensure that your system has sufficient entropy so that reads from /dev/random
do not block.

Also could we check `System.getProperty("os.name").startsWith("Windows") == false` rather than making the message itself conditional on Linux? Not sure if we want this at all on Windows or if we just drop the bit about `/dev/random`.

reply.body: Both suggestions sound good to me. I like the approach of checking for windows and adding the bit on /dev/random.

timeline.body: Isn't this the same as just using `getOutput()` since terminalLen is the len of `getOutput()`?

reply.body: The new call of installPlugin will cause more messages to come out, so it will advance the length of the output from the length I capture in terminalLen. I'm  trying to cut out the previous install output which shows the error, and compare what the successful install produced in the output.
MockTerminal has a `reset()` method to serve this purpose.
Ah I didn't know, I'll use that instead, thanks!
